findings.reason: The protected solution is rigorous, conventional, and interview-ready for a hard design problem. The sentinel-linked list, maximum heap, active-node map, monotonic identifiers, focused append/unlink/cleanup helpers, and operation dispatcher make each responsibility explicit without conflating stack order and maximum order.

The node before the tail is always the live stack top, and constant-time unlinking preserves the relative order of every survivor. Heap keys prioritize the greatest value and, for equal values, the greatest push identifier, which is the occurrence closest to the top. The active map contains exactly the linked nodes; ordinary pop removes only that membership, and cleanup later discards stale heap roots until the greatest live occurrence remains. Thus every operation returns and removes the contractually correct element, including duplicate maxima.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 716, Python, and the native MaxStack class operations. Authenticated source evidence confirms constructor initialization, push, pop, top, peekMax, popMax, nonmutating reads, topmost duplicate-maximum removal, O(1) top calls, O(log n) other calls, legal values from -10000000 through 10000000, at most 100000 operations, and the guarantee that every non-push operation has an element available.

The protected app classes and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065663898 are identical in node layout, sentinels, heap keys, active map, identifier assignment, lazy cleanup, list mutations, and all five public operations. The app adds only the solve operation dispatcher around that exact Accepted implementation.

A fresh run proved the former 16/64/256-operation tiers too small to distinguish the correct quadratic control reliably, so the same legal workload was recalibrated to 512, 2048, and 8192 operations. Each tier pushes descending values so every maximum remains deepest and then removes every value with popMax. The exact protected source passed all twelve ordinary cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent +0.01 and a 1.01x largest runtime ratio. A correct plain-list control that rescans for each maximum and shifts after interior removal passed every output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.41, distinguishing heap-indexed linked nodes from quadratic aggregate work without approaching the 100000-call boundary.

The Approach accurately derives the linked-list stack view, heap maximum view, identifier-based duplicate ordering, active-map bridge, and lazy-deletion invariant. Its O(q log q) total-time and O(q) space claims match the amortized cleanup accounting, protected implementation, and branch manifest.

The four-section modular Reference explains construction and all five operations, nonmutating reads, top-most duplicate-maximum removal, relative-order preservation, and the app adapter. It preserves the exact class-style source example, constructor and push null outputs, all ten explanation steps and intermediate stack states, and all three constraints. The provider's unheaded operation-level performance target remains in the branch-owned Required Complexity and Complexity detail artifacts, as required by the repository structure.

The authenticated live Premium statement directly verified exactly one fully explained example, no source images or tables, MaxStack initialization and five operations, top-most duplicate-maximum removal, O(1) top and O(log n) every other call, -10000000 <= x <= 10000000, at most 100000 calls, and a nonempty stack for pop, top, peekMax, and popMax. The hash-bound source_fidelity.json validates as verified with statement content SHA-256 c938b2b7ce91afdf9a483918c43ba3a303f1b9dfc4e4cacbba997e1c5faaeeb7.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly one example. Its exact pushes and calls appear first in source order through the app operation adapter, with the exact six non-push outputs; the two former repository-authored samples were retained as visible trials rather than misrepresented as source examples.

All twelve ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden duplicate-removal, multiple-stale-root, and single-element lifecycle behaviors were exposed, so cases.json no longer conceals any correctness behavior.

Contract boundaries cover -10000000 and 10000000, a single-element stack, removal down to an empty stack followed by a legal new push, and the nonempty precondition for every value-returning call. A separate generated workload exercises the exact 100000-call maximum with 50000 pushes and 50000 legal popMax calls without bloating an ordinary case.

Material behavior covers ordinary pop, top and peekMax without mutation, maxima at the top, middle, and bottom, duplicate maxima removed from topmost to bottommost, preservation of survivor order, negative values, interleaved reads and removals, and lazy deletion of one or several stale heap roots.

Expected results were checked against an independent list model across 280515 exhaustive legal operation sequences through length seven over values -1, 0, and 1, plus 500 seeded random legal traces and the 100000-call boundary workload. The protected app adapter and immutable native MaxStack agreed throughout and on every authored case and benchmark.
The recalibrated 512, 2048, and 8192-operation workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 16x, and make the correct plain-list rescan control fail only the scaling verdict.
